hook.line: Tomás needs a signed certificate for the cooperative, and official papers do not say *I*. They say *the undersigned*.
hook.es: El suscrito certifica que Tomás es el dueño del café.
hook.en: The undersigned certifies that Tomás is the owner of the café.

examples.es: El suscrito certifica que la señora Pérez trabaja en esta entidad.
examples.en: The undersigned certifies that Mrs Pérez works for this organisation.

examples.es: La suscrita certifica que Vale trabaja en el café.
examples.en: The undersigned (a woman) certifies that Vale works in the café.

examples.es: El suscrito hace constar que la reunión se pospuso.
examples.en: The undersigned records that the meeting was postponed.

examples.es: Los abajo firmantes hacemos constar nuestro desacuerdo.
examples.en: We, the undersigned, record our disagreement.

examples.es: Los abajo firmantes solicitamos una reunión de la junta.
examples.en: We, the undersigned, request a meeting of the board.

examples.es: La suscrita hace constar que recibió el aporte.
examples.en: The undersigned (a woman) records that she received the contribution.

rule:
Official papers hide the *I* behind a title.

*El suscrito* or *la suscrita* = the undersigned, one person (a man or a woman). The verb is third person: *certifica*, *hace constar*.

*Los abajo firmantes* = we, the undersigned. The verb is *we*: *hacemos constar*, *solicitamos*.

*Hacer constar* = to put on record. *Certificar* = to certify.

This is strictly written. Said aloud, it sounds like a joke.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the third-person self-reference of legal and administrative writing.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *El suscrito* or *La suscrita*, then type the whole sentence: ___ certifica que Vale trabaja en el café. (a woman writing)
yourTurn.answer: La suscrita certifica que Vale trabaja en el café.
yourTurn.why: A woman writing uses the feminine, *la suscrita*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *hacemos* or *hace*, then type the whole sentence: Los abajo firmantes ___ constar que no hubo quórum. (We record…)
yourTurn.answer: Los abajo firmantes hacemos constar que no hubo quórum.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: The undersigned (a man) records that the meeting was postponed.
yourTurn.answer: El suscrito hace constar que la reunión se pospuso.
yourTurn.why: One man: *el suscrito*, with a third-person verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: We, the undersigned, request a meeting of the board.
yourTurn.answer: Los abajo firmantes solicitamos una reunión de la junta.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: The undersigned (a woman) records that she received the contribution.
yourTurn.answer: La suscrita hace constar que recibió el aporte.
yourTurn.why: *Suscrita* for a woman, *hace constar* for the record.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a woman writing: El suscrito certifica que Tomás es el dueño del café.
yourTurn.answer: La suscrita certifica que Tomás es el dueño del café.
yourTurn.why: The article and the ending both change: *la suscrita*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a group: El suscrito hace constar que la reunión se pospuso.
yourTurn.answer: Los abajo firmantes hacemos constar que la reunión se pospuso.
yourTurn.why: A group is *los abajo firmantes*, and the verb becomes *we*.

pitfalls.wrong: El suscrito certificamos que Tomás es el dueño del café.
pitfalls.right: El suscrito certifica que Tomás es el dueño del café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *El suscrito* is one person in the third person, so *certifica*.

pitfalls.wrong: La suscrito certifica que Vale trabaja en el café.
pitfalls.right: La suscrita certifica que Vale trabaja en el café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A woman is *la suscrita*, with the *-a* ending.

pitfalls.wrong: Hola, Vale, el suscrito quiere un tinto.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *El suscrito* is for written documents; said aloud it sounds like a joke.

personal: Write a one-line certificate for a friend in the third person, starting with *El suscrito* or *La suscrita*.
